card.hook: Some places don't want a clever photo, and Pulse is one of them. People come here to pay their respects first, so keep your phone low-key and your pictures simple.
card.stand_here: Stand at the corner of South Orange Avenue and West Esther Street, at the southwest corner of the site by the Esther Street entrance. Face north-west: the old building lies that way, and this side-street angle is more open than the Orange Avenue frontage.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the whole scene. Use 0.5x only if you need more of the frontage, and keep the building away from the edges so the lines don't bend. Zoom 2x or 5x gives you a close, quiet frame of the names wall without walking up to it.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the building on one of the lines so the wall of photographs leads the eye along the frame.
card.best_time: Daylight gives the clearest view of the wall of photographs and the names. If you go after dark, use night mode and hold the phone steady against your body. The site is changing, so check the official site before you head over.
card.selfie_here: We're not suggesting a selfie spot here. A visitor guide advises against posed selfies with the site, so take a simple photo of what you see instead.
card.rules_and_safety: Personal photos are allowed at the memorial, but please keep them respectful. Posed selfies with the site and videos that use it as a backdrop are discouraged. Leave other visitors out of your frame where you can, and skip portrait mode and Live Photos, as a plain still photo suits the place better.
card.challenge: Take one thoughtful photo, then put your phone away and spend a quiet minute just looking.
card.good_to_know: Barbara Poma and Ron Legler opened Pulse at 1912 South Orange Avenue on 2 July 2004. Poma named it in memory of her brother John, who died from AIDS in 1991. On 12 June 2016, 49 people were killed and 58 injured here, the deadliest violence against LGBTQ people in US history. The City of Orlando bought the property in October 2023 and plans a permanent memorial, and demolition of the building began on 18 March 2026, so what you see may differ from this description.

selfie_research.notes: No selected spot: none of the pages I found names a place for a selfie with Pulse behind you, and the Anthem Orlando guide says selfies posed with the site are not appropriate, so I did not suggest one. The landmark itself has changed: the Anthem guide and WESH both say the original nightclub building was demolished in March 2026 for a permanent memorial, and the Anthem guide says the iconic sign was removed and is being preserved for the new memorial. The Forbes piece describes the planned design (a 49-foot tower at Orange Avenue and Esther Street, a Memorial Plaza on the old building footprint with a reflecting pool), but it is a plan, not a finished site, so I did not use it for a spot. For the 'ask someone' idea, the Orlando Escape page only gives entrances (South Orange Avenue by the Pulse sign, or Esther Street at the southwest corner), not a photo position. No page I found states rules on selfie sticks or tripods, so I have not reported any. Some visitor reviews on Tripadvisor mention 24-hour security against protest vandalism; I did not treat this as a visitor safety point.
